stories.delivered_paragraph: Paramount Skydance wants its antitrust trial over the proposed $111 billion Warner Bros. merger set for November, while a coalition of 12 states and the Writers Guild of America wants it to begin April 5, 2027. California and New York are among the states alleging the deal would reduce competition in cable and theatrical distribution; Paramount says it would strengthen its challenge to Netflix and Amazon. Timing is costly because Paramount will owe Warner shareholders $7 million a day from Sept. 30 until closing.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Fender’s claim of newly secured copyright protection for the Stratocaster guitar shape has triggered a fight with instrument makers including Yamaha and PRS Guitars. German lawyers sent cease-and-desist letters in May demanding that Strat-shaped guitars made by competitors be removed from the European market; some companies changed designs, while others are contesting the claim. The disputes could determine whether one of the industry’s most copied body styles can remain widely available outside Fender’s own products.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Researchers at Imperial College and Emlyon Business School say venture-backed startup founders appear more prone to securities fraud, examining SEC and Justice Department civil and criminal cases from 2000 through 2023. A separate University of Toronto study identified 654 fraud cases involving U.S. VC-backed startups over the same period, while stressing that fraud remains rare overall. The research puts scrutiny on investor incentives and startup norms that can reward aggressive growth claims before a company’s business is fully proven.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Indian consumers spent a record $345 million on mobile apps in the second quarter, up 35% from a year earlier, as subscriptions for generative AI, streaming and productivity services gained traction. Sensor Tower says revenue per download has more than doubled over the past three and a half years even as quarterly downloads have held near 6.3 billion since 2023. The shift gives app developers a more viable paid market in a country long defined by huge download volumes but weak monetization.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Alphabet and Tesla reported negative cash flow in their latest quarter, while Meta’s cash generation fell 91%, underscoring how expensive the technology industry’s AI buildout has become. Companies are committing enormous sums to data centers and computing equipment as memory costs rise, even when their core businesses remain profitable. Investors now have to judge whether the spending will produce durable AI revenue quickly enough to justify the pressure on cash generation.

stories.delivered_paragraph: President Trump’s defense of a proposed Justice Department “anti-weaponization” compensation fund has renewed resistance to confirming acting Attorney General Todd Blanche. Republican Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis have said they will not support Blanche until the department formally rules out elements of the fund, despite Trump saying it is dead; Tillis argued Trump’s comments suggested otherwise. The dispute leaves the Justice Department’s top job unsettled and centers on concerns over using taxpayer money to compensate people alleging government mistreatment.

stories.delivered_paragraph: MarketWatch highlights a less discussed effect of delaying Social Security claims: waiting until age 70 raises not only the monthly benefit but also the dollar value of future cost-of-living adjustments. The higher payment is designed to reflect a later claim, but it also creates a larger inflation-linked income stream for retirees who can afford to wait. That trade-off matters as households weigh claiming strategies against Social Security’s longer-term funding pressures.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Rescuers recovered the remains of U.S. climber Mallory Geis after an avalanche struck a 10-person expedition on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, near the Chinese border. Authorities also identified the bodies of climbers from Oman and Nepal, while bad weather complicated recovery efforts and one person remained unaccounted for. The search will resume when teams can safely reach the high-altitude site, where drones have spotted additional possible victims.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Hamas said it will disarm only after Israel fulfills earlier ceasefire commitments, qualifying President Trump’s assertion that a U.S.-brokered Gaza agreement had achieved a breakthrough on disarmament. The response leaves a central element of any longer-term settlement unresolved, since Hamas’s weapons have been a core Israeli and U.S. demand. The disagreement shows that even if ceasefire terms are being discussed, the parties still differ over sequencing and what each side must deliver first.

stories.delivered_paragraph: An estimated 60,000 people from Morocco crossed into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta over 24 hours, an unprecedented surge for a territory with about 83,000 residents. Dozens died attempting the crossing, though Spanish officials said more than 48,000 migrants had voluntarily returned to Morocco by Friday evening. The episode again exposes Ceuta’s vulnerability as a gateway to Europe and puts pressure on Spain and Morocco to contain a rapidly developing humanitarian emergency.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A U.S. company is delivering medical supplies by drone in Rwanda, helping clinics receive urgent items faster across difficult terrain. But NPR reports that the technology cannot solve shortages of staff, facilities and other basics in a weak health-care system. The experience is a reminder that drone logistics can improve access at the margins, yet its benefits depend on whether local clinics have the capacity to diagnose, store and use the supplies delivered.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” took in a record $72 million in domestic previews and is projected by industry estimates to earn roughly $270 million to more than $330 million over its opening weekend. Deadline reported an opening-day range of $167 million to $173 million, above “Avengers: Endgame’s” $157.4 million first-day record. The debut would give theaters a major summer boost, though its final weekend ranking depends on whether early demand holds through Sunday.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Toronto Tempo acquired Connecticut Sun forward Aneesah Morrow for the rights to Maria Kliundikova and a 2028 second-round pick. Morrow, the No. 7 selection in last year’s draft, averaged 11.6 points and 8.9 rebounds in 23.2 minutes over 20 games this season, mostly off the bench, and posted nine double-doubles. The deal gives Toronto’s expansion roster a young frontcourt player with proven rebounding production while Connecticut adds future flexibility.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Atlanta’s ONE Musicfest has canceled its 2026 event after 16 years, saying it will use the pause to redesign the festival rather than repeat its established format. The festival has built a reputation for pairing major rap and R&B veterans with newer performers; last year’s lineup included Future, Mary J. Blige, Doechii and Clipse. Organizers have not announced a return date, leaving a gap in Atlanta’s festival calendar while they develop what they call the event’s next iteration.

stories.delivered_paragraph: FIFA’s disputed World Cup plans and threats of boycotts by some countries risk spilling into the 2027 Women’s World Cup, ESPN reports. The prospect of a major tournament being affected comes after years of investment and growth in women’s soccer, where reliable global showcases are crucial for audiences, sponsors and players. Any boycott or organizing conflict would shift attention from the competition itself and could disrupt momentum the women’s game has worked to build.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet added nearly $1.5 trillion in combined market value this week after strong cloud results and continued or higher AI spending forecasts persuaded investors that returns may be emerging. Microsoft gained more than $600 billion, while Amazon and Alphabet each added over $400 billion; meanwhile Apple lost more than $350 billion as a memory shortage hurt its outlook. The sharp split shows markets are rewarding companies that can tie AI investment to revenue while punishing unclear payoffs and supply pressures.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The S&P 500 finished July lower for the first time since 2014 after a volatile final stretch, with chip stocks leading the retreat. MarketWatch described the decline as the semiconductor sector’s worst month in 24 years, a sharp reversal for an industry that has been central to the market’s AI-driven gains. The pullback raises the risk that the broader index becomes more vulnerable if investors continue reassessing lofty expectations for technology and AI-related earnings.
